title: Fiado
goal: Be given credit at the shop, which means being trusted
culture: Fiado is credit in a school exercise book behind the counter, with no interest and no paperwork. Being given it is not a financial event, it is a social one: it says you are somebody who lives here and will be walking past tomorrow.

beats.en: Could you put it on credit?
beats.good: Fiado is credit, in a notebook, with nothing signed. Asking for it is asking to be counted as a neighbour rather than a customer.
Ideay is the most Nicaraguan noise there is — surprise, greeting, disbelief, delight — and the tone does all of the work. Here it means: really? Thanks.

beats.es: Le apunto aquí en el cuaderno, ¿va?
beats.en: Yes, put it down for me.
beats.good: Me lo apunta — put it down for me. That exercise book is the entire credit system of the barrio and it works better than most.

beats.en: I’ll pay you tomorrow. My word.
beats.good: Say the day and then keep it. The thing that ends fiado is never being poor — it is not turning up.
